asset_label: underwater bridge substructure (pier, pile, footing, abutment, channel bed) seen in an ROV camera frame or a rendered imaging-sonar frame
source_note: Two families of rows. (1) Scour Condition Rating bands from the 2022 NBIS interval rules, 23 CFR 650.311(b), read on the ecfr.io mirror https://ecfr.io/Title-23/Section-650.311 (docs/research/10_multisensor_scope.md section 1.1 [1]); the SNBI item is B.C.11 Scour Condition on the 0-9 scale (R10 [7], secondary: SNBI PDF not fetched). (2) Element damage grades quoted from the NYC EDC Waterfront Facilities Maintenance Management System Inspection Guidelines Manual (Oct 2019), Tables 3-3 to 3-6, https://edc.nyc/sites/default/files/2019-10/NYCEDC-WFMMS-Inspection-Guidelines-Manual.pdf, as transcribed in docs/research/05_damage_grading_standards.md section 5.2; the 'Good' row reuses the manual's section 3.3 overall-rating term because the element tables start at Minor. FHWA position on sonar (NBIS Q&A Q313-11, updated 2024-04-05, https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/bridge/nbis2022/qanda/08.cfm): imaging technology 'can supplement' Level I, but 'The Level II portion of the UWI is still to be performed by an underwater bridge inspection diver', and sonars 'have not demonstrated the ability to identify some smaller scale elements of substructure condition'. A grade from this rubric is therefore a Level I screening aid, never a Level II result. Unified mapping is the team's own (mirrors bridge_mbei.json / corrosion_cs.json: first defect grade S1, then S2, S3, with S4 reserved for breakage or undermining); rows whose threshold could not be sourced say [team-proposed, validate].

rows.criterion: No problems or only minor problems noted. Structural elements may show some very minor deterioration, but no overstressing observed. (NYC EDC WFMMS section 3.3 overall rating 'Good', reused as the no-defect element state [team-proposed, validate])
mechanical/impact spalls; cracks up to 1/32 in (NYC EDC WFMMS Table 3-4 'Minor'; crack vocabulary: 'Hairline - Crack width less than 1/32 in.')
"Structural cracks up to 1/16 in."; "Corrosion cracks up to 1/4 in."; "rounding of corners up to 1 in. deep" (NYC EDC WFMMS Table 3-4 'Moderate')
"Structural cracks 1/16 in. to 1/4 in. ... partial breakages (structural spalls)"; "Corrosion cracks wider than 1/4 in. and open spalls" (NYC EDC WFMMS Table 3-4 'Advanced')

"Structural cracks wider than 1/4 in. or complete breakage"; "over 30 percent of diameter loss for any main reinforcing bar"; "Loss of over 30 percent of cross section" (NYC EDC WFMMS Table 3-4 'Severe')
"impact spalls up to 0.5 in. deep"; "Structural cracks up to 1/32 in." (NYC EDC WFMMS Table 3-5 'Minor')
"Structural cracks 1/32 in. to 1/8 in."; "Any corrosion cracks generated by strands" (NYC EDC WFMMS Table 3-5 'Moderate')
"cracks wider than 1/16 in."; softening up to 1 in. deep (NYC EDC WFMMS Table 3-5 'Advanced')
"Structural cracks wider than 1/8 in. and at least partial breakage"; "Corrosion spalls over any prestressing steel" (NYC EDC WFMMS Table 3-5 'Severe')

"<50 percent of perimeter ... affected by corrosion"; "Loss of thickness up to 15 percent"; corrosion descriptor Minor "light surface corrosion with no apparent loss of section" (NYC EDC WFMMS Table 3-3 'Minor')

">50 percent of perimeter"; "Loss of thickness 15 to 30 percent"; corrosion descriptor Moderate "loose and flaking with some pitting ... measurable but not significant loss of section" (NYC EDC WFMMS Table 3-3 'Moderate')
"Loss of nominal thickness 30 to 50" percent; "Partial loss of flange edges" (NYC EDC WFMMS Table 3-3 'Advanced')

Severe steel row not extracted from the manual in R05 (more than 50 percent thickness loss or buckling implied); corrosion descriptor Severe "Heavy, stratified corrosion ... Significant loss of section." [team-proposed, validate against NYC EDC WFMMS Table 3-3]
"Checks, splits and gouges less than 0.5 in. wide" (NYC EDC WFMMS Table 3-6 'Minor')
"Checks and splits wider than 0.5 in."; "Remaining diameter loss up to 15 percent"; "Cross section area loss up to 25 percent"; marine borer evidence (NYC EDC WFMMS Table 3-6 'Moderate')
"Remaining diameter loss 15 to 30 percent"; "Cross section area loss 25 to 50 percent" (NYC EDC WFMMS Table 3-6 'Advanced')
"Remaining diameter reduced by more than 30 percent"; "Cross section area loss more than 50 percent"; "Partial or complete breakage" (NYC EDC WFMMS Table 3-6 'Severe')

Scour Condition Rating 7 to 9: within the extended-interval band '(A)(3) Scour Condition Rating item is satisfactory or better, coded six (6) or greater' (23 CFR 650.311(b)(1)(iii)); the split of 7-9 from 6 follows the 0-9 mapping in bridge_nbi.json [team-proposed, validate]. Channel bed and footings visible with no scour hole, exposure or undermining.

Scour Condition Rating 6, the lowest code still 'satisfactory or better, coded six (6) or greater' (23 CFR 650.311(b)(1)(iii)(A)(3)): minor scour or bed lowering without footing exposure [team-proposed, validate]

Scour Condition Rating 4 or 5: neither the reduced-interval trigger (3 or less) nor the extended-interval condition (6 or greater) applies, so the default applies: '(b)(1)(i): Each bridge must be inspected at regular intervals not to exceed 60 months' (23 CFR 650.311). Scour hole or partial footing exposure present [team-proposed, validate]

'(B)(3) The observed scour condition is three (3) or less, as recorded by the Scour Condition Rating item' triggers the reduced interval 'not to exceed 24 months' (23 CFR 650.311(b)(1)(ii)); 'Critical Findings can also be triggered by extreme scour conditions (Scour Condition B.C.11 rated 3 or below)' (Geocadra SNBI summary, https://www.geocadra.com/en/standards/fhwa-nbis-snbi, secondary). Undermined footing, exposed piles or bed lowered below the footing.

unified_note: Severe with breakage of a primary member, or SCR 0-3 with visible undermining or tilting, maps to S4 (escalate). Sonar frames (ARIS Explorer 3000 class: 3 to 19 mm downrange resolution, R10 section 1.3) can support the scour family and the Advanced/Severe element grades (extent and geometry) but cannot resolve the 1/32 to 1/8 in crack classes: on a sonar frame, crack-width rows are not_measurable and the grade comes from extent, exposure or breakage only. Marine growth must be removed on a sampling basis before section loss is rated (WFMMS inspection tables): a frame with growth over the element cannot be graded for thickness loss.
measurement_note: crack_width_mm and section_loss_pct require a scale reference or thickness data; the sonar range and frequency and the ROV stand-off must be passed as metadata next to the frame (R10 section 10).

flags.section_loss: set on Moderate steel and every Advanced grade
flags.load_posting_review: set on every Severe grade and on SCR 0-3
flags.not_measurable: set when width, thickness or depth cannot be measured from the frame
